# ===========================================================================
# GESVR - HEAD-AIM VR MODE
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configured to play the game properly in VR without motion weapons: full
# stereo, head tracking, head aim, floating HUD, gun in its normal Source
# position. This is the Luke Ross style of VR conversion, and it avoids the
# entire motion-weapon problem area (skewing, snap-to-head, offset muzzle
# flash) which is not close to production quality.
#
# To go back to motion weapons later, set:
#   AimMode=gun / MotionControls=true / WeaponSetupHook=true
#   ViewmodelRenderablePatch=true / ShowWristHUD=true
#
# This whole file hot-reloads: save it while the game runs and changes apply in
# about a second.
# ===========================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# How the stereo image reaches the headset.
#   compositor : real per-eye submit with the correct asymmetric frustum crop.
#                This is the one that should feel like you are IN the level.
#   sbs        : the old head-locked side-by-side quad. Stereo, but it reads as
#                a giant 3D television. Kept as a fallback.
#   both       : compositor plus the quad, for an A/B in one session.
# This file is hot-reloaded -- save it while the game runs and it takes effect.
DisplayMode=compositor

# Crops each eye's true asymmetric frustum out of the shared wide render.
# Turning this off reproduces the old too-big-world look; it is the single
# biggest contributor to correct VR scale.
UseEyeFrustumCrop=true

# The horizontal half of that crop is unambiguous. The vertical half depends on
# a sign convention that can only be settled in a headset: if the world sits too
# high or too low, set this false and only the horizontal crop applies.
UseVerticalCrop=true

# Size of the per-eye render targets (EyeRenderTargets below), as a multiple
# of what the headset asks for once the frustum crop is allowed for. 1.0 is
# about native after the crop; above 1 is supersampling, which is the only
# anti-aliasing the eyes get on this path (see AntiAliasing). Capped at 3072
# pixels a side. Measured 2026-09-28: 3072x3072 targets cost no address space
# at all -- they live in GPU memory -- and about 0.2 ms over 2688x2688.
EyeRenderScale=1.0

# Floating menu panel: how big the game's menus look, and how far away they
# float. The two are independent -- the width below is the panel's width at
# 1.6 m and is scaled with the distance, so moving a menu does not resize it.
# 2.0 is the 100% the VR Settings panel shows. Both hot-reload.
MenuWidthMeters=2.0
MenuDistanceMeters=1.2

# Render each eye into its own render target at the headset's own resolution
# and shape, instead of into the game window.
#
# The window path renders each eye into a 16:9 window and crops it, so every
# eye gets about 1390x1440 useful pixels however good the headset is, and
# anything drawn flat on the screen (the HUD, the radar) comes out 1.84x
# stretched. This path gives each eye roughly its native ~2900x3000.
#
# It was "broken" for a month because the right eye only drew its top 58%.
# The cause was never the right eye: shaderapidx9's SetViewports clamps every
# viewport to the WINDOW's size, so any target bigger than the window was cut
# to its top-left corner (viewport_clamp.h has the disassembly). With the clamp
# lifted for the eye passes both eyes fill completely, the game survives a map
# change, and it costs ~1.4 ms a frame and no address space.
#
# What changes: GE:S's own HUD is kept OUT of the eyes, because on this build
# it can only be drawn at the view's size and the in-eye copy is what was
# stretched. The watch shows health, armour, ammo, time, weapon and kills; the
# radar is the one thing that has nowhere to go. false = the old window path.
EyeRenderTargets=true

# Head-tracking latency fix. Each frame goes to SteamVR BEFORE the mod waits
# for the next head pose, with the pose it was rendered at attached, so
# SteamVR's last-moment correction lines the image up with your head. Before
# this, every frame arrived one frame late and labelled with the wrong pose:
# the world trailed your head by ~14 ms when you turned. false = the old order,
# only for comparing the two.
HeadPoseFix=true

# IVModelRender vtable index of DrawModelExecute -- the hook that lets the mod
# move the weapon onto your hand. This was NEVER hooked before: offsets.h has an
# L4D2 byte signature that GE:S's engine does not match, which is why the gun
# could only ever follow your view angles. The index was measured in game with a
# per-slot call counter: [18]=128689 and [19]=128291 were the two hottest and
# differ by 398 -- Source's DrawModelSetup/DrawModelExecute pair.
ModelDrawExecuteSlot=19

# The other half of the pair. The weapon must be MOVED here, not at Execute:
# the log showed the viewmodel arriving at Execute with its origin exactly equal
# to the view origin, and changing it there does nothing because the bone
# matrices are already built. Setup runs first and takes the info by non-const
# reference, so a change lands in both the bones and the draw.
ModelDrawSetupSlot=18

# OFF - hooking slot 18 with a guessed DrawModelSetup signature crashed on the
# first stereo pass. The argument list does not match, so calling through
# corrupts the stack immediately. Do not enable until SetupProbe confirms the
# real signature.
WeaponSetupHook=false

# Redirects the viewmodel's GetRenderOrigin/GetRenderAngles to the controller
# pose. Writing ModelRenderInfo_t::origin provably does NOT move the gun (the
# write fires with a 27-unit displacement and nothing happens) because the root
# transform is built by SetupBones from these two accessors instead.
# Set false if the weapon renders wrong or the game becomes unstable.
ViewmodelRenderablePatch=false

# true  = the hand pose is applied only during the weapon's draw call. Cleaner,
#         but the gun snaps back to your head on any draw path we do not
#         intercept -- which is what happens while firing.
# false = the pose stays applied permanently. The gun stays on your hand through
#         firing, at the cost of the engine also using it for culling and
#         attachments, which is what made it warp.
#
# NEITHER IS CORRECT. Both are symptoms of a render-only override: the model is
# drawn at your hand while the weapon ENTITY still sits at your head, so the mesh
# ends up spanning two transforms (the stretching) and effects spawn from the old
# position (the offset muzzle flash). Try both and use whichever bothers you
# less; the real fix is to move the entity, which is the next piece of work.
ViewmodelScopedPose=true

# Safe naked capture of slot 18's actual arguments. Costs nothing; turn off once
# the signature is known.
SetupProbe=false

# Motion trace. Samples the whole hand -> weapon chain 4x/second while in a map.
# Run the calibration sequence in HANDOFF.md and send the log; each stage can
# then be verified independently instead of guessed at.
MotionDebug=false

# Re-run the slot counter (conflicts with the hook above; diagnosis only).
VtableProbe=false
# ^^^ TURN THIS ON FOR RESOLUTION ^^^
# Confirmed from the 21:26 log: "stereo pass #0 eyeRT=0 size=1280x720". With
# this off, each eye is captured from the 1280x720 window backbuffer and then
# upscaled to a ~2496x2688 headset eye -- that IS the blurriness. With it on,
# each eye renders into its own render target at true HMD resolution.
# This file hot-reloads: you can flip it while standing in a map and see the
# difference immediately. If anything renders wrong, flip it back.

# Only used when DisplayMode=sbs or both.
SbsWidthMeters=3.17
SbsDistance=1.0

# Menu pointer. Win32 posts real mouse messages to the game window and is the
# reliable path. The VGUI-internal path calls into a vgui2 vtable whose 2007
# layout is unconfirmed -- leave it off unless you are testing it.
# Menus are pointed at with the controller only (the right hand, or the left
# with LeftHanded=true). There is no head pointer any more.

# If the in-game character menu hangs the game again, set this false. It stops
# the pointer from touching the OS cursor, so you lose the in-map cursor
# but keep a stable game.
MenuDriveCursor=true

# Draw our own cursor marker into the menu image where SteamVR's laser is not
# on the panel (in-map menus). Source's cursor is a hardware cursor and never
# reaches the headset, so without this those menus have no cursor at all.
# It follows the controller, and is hidden while SteamVR's own dot is showing.
DrawMenuCursor=true

# Aiming reticle drawn straight into each eye. The game's own crosshair never
# reaches the headset -- +crosshair 1 is set, but the 2D HUD is not part of what
# we capture. In head-aim mode you aim with the centre of your view, so a centre
# reticle is both correct and independent of the game's HUD.
VRReticle=true

MenuInputWin32=true
MenuInputVguiInternal=false

# Kill switch for ALL OS-level cursor driving (SetCursorPos, SetForegroundWindow,
# PostMessage). Set false to rule the whole menu-input subsystem out at once.
# (duplicate of the setting above, removed) MenuDriveCursor=true

# SetCursorPos moves the real Windows cursor. It is a system-wide call that can
# transact with the desktop input thread; PostMessage cannot block. If the game
# freezes shortly after the menu appears, set this false -- Source's inputsystem
# consumes WM_MOUSEMOVE on its own, so the laser may still work without it.
MenuUseSetCursorPos=true

# Keep the game window on a single monitor. At higher render resolutions the
# window was reported spanning both displays. Only the captured backbuffer
# reaches the headset, so a stretched desktop window costs nothing visually, but
# it is disruptive to work around. Handled on the input worker thread, which
# owns all USER32 - doing window work from the render thread is what deadlocked
# the game earlier in this project.
KeepWindowOnPrimaryMonitor=false

# How a menu click is delivered. The freeze happens immediately after a click is
# posted, every time. PostMessage synthesises a message with no hardware input
# behind it; VGUI calls SetMouseCapture on button-down, and a synthetic press
# whose physical button was never down can leave it waiting for a release that
# cannot arrive. SendInput goes through the real input queue like a physical
# mouse. If the game freezes the moment you click, try true.
MenuClickViaSendInput=false

# How often the menu talks to the SteamVR compositor, in milliseconds.
# This is NOT just a keepalive. OpenVR's Vulkan Submit drains the graphics
# queue, so its cost is proportional to how much game rendering piled up since
# the last submit. At the old 500ms spacing the engine free-ran at ~225fps,
# leaving ~110 frames to drain -- an 83-150ms freeze every half second, which
# is the stutter you were feeling. 33ms cuts that to about 5ms.
#   33  = default, smooth
#   11  = display cadence, smoothest; try it if 33 is stable
#   500 = old behaviour, for comparison
MenuKeepaliveMs=33


# SteamVR's desktop mirror window. It competes with the game for Win32 focus,
# and Source throttles rendering hard (and mutes audio) whenever its own window
# is not the active app. A VR mod gains nothing from it. Leave off.
ShowMirrorWindow=false

# How often to re-suppress the SteamVR Theater overlay, in milliseconds.
# Each pass is ~10 IPC round-trips to vrserver. 0 = every frame (old behaviour).
TheaterHideThrottleMs=2000

EnableNetVR=true
# head = look and shoot with the headset
# gun  = weapons follow the right controller (default)
AimMode=head
MotionControls=false

# Gun grip correction, degrees. A controller's forward axis is not a barrel
# axis; this rotates the weapon down into a natural grip. 45 is what L4D2VR and
# HaloCEVR use. If the gun points too high, raise it; too low, lower it.
# Set 0 to aim straight down the controller's own axis.
# Confirmed in play: at 0, pointing straight ahead shoots ~45 degrees HIGH.
# Positive pitch is DOWN in Source, so 45 brings the shot onto your aim.
# Nudge in 5-degree steps if it is slightly off; this hot-reloads.
# Viewmodel FOV. 0 = use the world FOV, which for the HMD's superset frustum is
# ~106 degrees -- very wide, and it drags the weapon toward the centre of your
# view and makes it disagree with the world-space muzzle effect.
# Try 54-75 to put the gun back where Source normally draws it. Hot-reloads, so
# nudge it while looking at the gun.
ViewmodelFov=0

GunGripAngle=45.0

# Per-weapon viewmodel poses from the table in weapons.cpp (pp7, dd44, klobb,
# ar33, rcp90, sniper, shotguns, knife, grenades...). That table was completely
# unreachable until now -- its only caller had no call sites -- so every weapon
# used one generic pose.
PerWeaponOffsets=false

# Two-handed grip: bring the off hand up near the barrel and the gun aims along
# the line between your hands. Skipped for melee, dual-wieldables and throwables.
TwoHandedGrip=true

# HOLD the off-hand grip button to go two-handed, HaloCEVR-style. Previously it
# engaged purely on hand distance, which fired whenever your hands drifted near
# each other. Set false to go back to distance-only.
TwoHandedNeedsGrip=true

# Fine gun placement relative to your hand, in Source units (1 unit ~= 1 inch),
# as forward,right,up. Positive forward pulls the weapon back toward you.
# --- Weapon alignment -------------------------------------------------------
# Hand tracking is live, so these two dial the gun into your hand. Both
# hot-reload: edit, save, and the change lands in about a second while you are
# standing in a map. Neither affects where bullets go -- aim is driven
# separately by GunGripAngle, which is already correct.
#
# Position, in Source units (~1 inch), as forward,right,up relative to your
# hand. Positive forward pushes the gun away from you.
ViewmodelOffset=0,0,0

# Rotation of the WEAPON MODEL only, as pitch,yaw,roll in degrees.
# If the gun looks rotated wrong in your hand, adjust here, not GunGripAngle.
ViewmodelAngleOffset=0,0,0
TurnSpeed=0.35
SnapTurning=false
SnapTurnAngle=45.0
LeftHanded=false
# World scale, game units per metre. Also sets how tall you feel: eye height
# feels like 64 / VRScale metres standing. 40 is life size; lower = taller.
VRScale=40.0
# Lifts the camera, in metres, if standing play feels too short. Camera only:
# shots still come from the game's eye height and the gun stays where it was,
# so every shot lands this far BELOW the reticle at any range. Keep it small.
HeightOffsetMeters=0.0
# Left grip = GE:S aim mode (+aimmode). With a scoped weapon the game zooms,
# and this carries the zoom into the headset by magnifying the whole view.
# false = aim mode still works, but the view never zooms.
ScopeZoom=true

# Zoomed in, the gun eases toward your hand instead of copying every tremor,
# so the magnified view is steady enough to aim. Stronger the more it zooms.
# 0 = off, 1 = default, 2 = steadier but slower to follow.
ScopeSmoothing=1.0

# Zooming, with the gun in your hand:
#   AR33 / KF7: hold them with both hands (off-hand grip), then pull the
#     off-hand trigger to zoom. The whole view zooms, as before.
#   Sniper rifle: hold it with both hands and its scope shows a zoomed picture
#     inside the lens; your view does not zoom. SniperScope=false = old zoom.
# Lining the lens up with the model's scope (game units, ~2.5 cm each):
#   ScopeLensBack   how far back from the muzzle, along the barrel
#   ScopeLensUp     how far above the barrel
#   ScopeLensRadius how big the glass is
# ScopeMagnification: 0 = the game's own sniper zoom, or e.g. 4 for 4x.
SniperScope=true
ScopeLensBack=24
ScopeLensUp=3.4
ScopeLensRadius=0.9
ScopeMagnification=0
# GE:S draws the first-person gun at the desktop window's shape, which in the
# headset stretched it tall and skewed it. true corrects that for the gun at
# your head (face aim) too; the gun in hand is always corrected.
FixViewmodelAspect=true
# Face aim: how far the gun at your head sits out to the lower right. 1 puts
# it where GE:S fires its muzzle flash and tracers from; 0 is straight in
# front of your face.
FaceAimGunSpread=1.0
# The game HUD in the headset: off, hurt (flash it when you take damage or are
# low) or always. The Show HUD button works in every mode. Also in VR Settings.
GameHUD=always
# Kills (yours called out: YOU KILLED / KILLED BY) and round start/end pop up
# on the watch for a few seconds, and GE:S's own kill feed is kept off the view.
# With the watch on, the round timer, ammo count and weapon list are also taken
# off GE:S's HUD, since the watch shows them. Also in VR Settings > Display.
WatchKillFeed=true
# The grenade and the mines are the only viewmodels with a left arm, and it
# carries GoldenEye's Seamaster. true puts that arm on your off-hand
# controller instead of dragging it along with the gun hand; the grenade or
# mine itself stays in your gun hand. Offsets are in the hand's own frame
# (forward,right,up and pitch,yaw,roll), like the weapon positions.
LeftHandOnController=true
LeftHandOffset=5.5,-0.5,4
LeftHandAngle=45,-65,-127.5
# Tune them in the headset like a weapon: VR Settings > Weapons > Adjust
# position, then numpad 7 to switch to the off hand (0 saves them here).
# With that arm drawn, the watch face sits on the Seamaster modelled on its
# wrist, and stays there afterwards, instead of at WatchOffset.
WatchFollowModel=true
# Switch weapons the moment you press (sets GE:S's hud_fastswitch 1): its
# pick-then-fire weapon list is a 2D panel you cannot see in the headset.
WeaponFastSwitch=true
# Numpad adjustment of where the held weapon sits in your hand (free aim).
# 8/2 4/6 9/3 move, 5 switches to rotate, +/- step size, 0 saves to
# VR/weapons.txt, . resets the held weapon. Also in VR Settings > Weapons.
WeaponTuning=false
# Texture filtering set on the game when a map loads: 4, 8 or 16 times
# anisotropic plus trilinear (sharp floors and walls at an angle), or 0 to
# leave the game's own Filtering mode alone. Also in VR Settings > Graphics.
TextureFiltering=16
# GE:S's bloom (the glow around bright lights). false looks crisper.
Bloom=true

# GE:S's own Advanced Video settings, mirrored into VR Settings > Graphics and
# > Detail because its options dialog cannot be worked from inside a headset:
# clicks never reach the Advanced sub-dialog, they fire the gun instead, and
# there is no way back out of it without killing the game.
#
# -1 everywhere means "say nothing", which leaves GE:S exactly as you left it.
#
# TextureDetail is by far the biggest memory cost, and memory is what decides
# whether a map loads at all -- watch the meter on the Graphics tab. It and
# ModelDetail throw away and reload every texture / model when they change,
# which is a crash with a map already up, so both are applied at the menu.
# mat_picmip: 0 high, 1 medium, 2 low.
TextureDetail=-1
# r_rootlod: 0 high, 1 medium, 2 low.
ModelDetail=-1
# mat_reducefillrate: 0 high, 1 low.
ShaderDetail=-1
# 0 simple, 1 reflect the world, 2 reflect everything.
WaterDetail=-1
# r_shadowrendertotexture: 0 blobs, 1 shaped.
ShadowDetail=-1
# Anti-aliasing (mat_antialias): 0 off, 2 or 4 for MSAA, -1 to leave it alone.
# The mod never applies this one -- changing it resets the D3D device under a
# live compositor -- so Launch-GESVR reads it from here and passes it on the
# command line. It takes effect the NEXT time you launch.
#
# WITH EyeRenderTargets ON THIS DOES NOT REACH THE HEADSET. MSAA applies to the
# backbuffer, and the eyes render into texture targets, which D3D9 cannot
# multisample -- measured 2026-09-28, 2x MSAA leaves the eye images exactly as
# jagged, once exposure is normalised. It then only smooths the desktop window
# and the menus, at a cost; 0 is the sensible setting. The eyes' own anti-
# aliasing is their resolution (raise EyeRenderScale to supersample).
#
# An earlier note here costed MSAA in address space (28 / 56 / 113 MB). That was
# wrong: render targets live in GPU memory and do not touch the 2 GB at all.
AntiAliasing=-1
# false = the normal death camera (sets GE:S's ge_fp_ragdoll 0) instead of the
# first-person one riding the ragdoll's head.
DeathCamFirstPerson=false
# How far the death curtain is stretched across your view.
BloodCurtainScale=2.6
# Aim mode (also in VR Settings): false = face aim, shoot where you look;
# true = free aim, the gun is in your right hand and fires where it points.
# Free aim also hides GE:S's own aim-mode crosshair, which is pinned to the
# centre of your view and would disagree with the gun.
TrackedWeapon=true
# With the gun in hand, shots go where the barrel points and the reticle sits
# on the spot it will hit. false = shots follow your head as before.
AimWithGun=true
# With the gun in hand and the slappers or hunting knife out, a fast chop
# of the right controller attacks; with the throwing knife, a flick throws it
# where the blade was pointing just before the flick. SwingSpeed is how fast,
# in metres per second: raise it if ordinary movement sets it off, lower it if
# chops are missed.
SwingMelee=true
SwingSpeed=2.0
# Throwing knife: the swing is detected as your hand starts moving, which is
# too early to let go -- the blade is still pointing back at you. The throw is
# released when your hand passes its fastest and begins to slow, or this many
# milliseconds after the swing started, whichever comes first. Raise it to let
# the knife go later in the swing, lower it to release sooner.
ThrowReleaseMs=150
# Which way a thrown knife goes, decided at the fastest moment of your swing:
# 0.0 = where your hand was travelling, 1.0 = where your hand was pointing
# (which is what the throw guide draws). An overhand throw curves downward, so
# pure motion throws low; pure pointing ignores the swing. Halfway by default.
ThrowAimMix=0.5
# Throw guide: with a grenade, throwing knife or mine in hand, a thin dotted
# path from your hand to a slightly bigger dot where it will first land, in the
# reticle colour. For a grenade cooked until its fuse would run out in the air,
# the path stops at the burst point; the end dot turns red if that blast would
# catch you. Thrown items fly where your hand points, so the path you see is
# the path it flies.
ThrowGuide=true
# Slappers and knives are placed by their hand. MeleeHideArm shows only the
# hand (the flat-screen arm otherwise runs back into your chest); set false
# for the full arm. MeleeAngleOffset tilts the hand as pitch,yaw,roll degrees.
MeleeHideArm=true
MeleeAngleOffset=0,0,0
# Multiplies your real eye separation. Above 1 exaggerates depth but makes
# the world feel smaller (you taller); leave at 1 for true scale.
IPDScale=1.0
HideArms=true
HudDistance=1.3
HudSize=1.1
# The floating HUD panel shows the WHOLE captured frame, so switching it on
# would hang a duplicate of the game in front of you. The 2D HUD is very likely
# already inside the stereo image, because our eye capture happens after
# CViewRender::RenderView has drawn it. Leave this off; if you find you cannot
# see health and ammo in the headset, set it true and we will crop the panel to
# just the HUD region instead.
HudAlwaysVisible=false

# Q-branch wrist watch on the off hand: GoldenEye 64 health (left) and armour
# (right) bars round a green screen with weapon, ammo and round time. It turns
# to face you. Also in the in-game VR Settings panel.
ShowWristHUD=true
# false = only while you look at your wrist; true = all the time.
WatchAlwaysVisible=false
# "Looking at it" = hand within this many metres and this close to the centre
# of view (dot product; 1 = dead centre).
WristLookMaxDistance=0.6
WristLookMinDot=0.45
# Watch face diameter in metres.
WatchWidth=0.10
# Where it sits relative to the off-hand controller, in metres, as
# forward,left,up. Negative forward is back towards your wrist.
WatchOffset=-0.13,0,0.04

# Health bars also flash in front of the HMD when you take a hit
HurtHUDWidth=0.55
HurtHUDDistance=0.85
HurtHUDSeconds=2.5
HurtHealthThreshold=80
HurtHUDUMin=0.00
HurtHUDVMin=0.78
HurtHUDUMax=0.50
HurtHUDVMax=1.00

# Aiming reticle arm length as a fraction of eye height. 0.006 is small.
VRReticleSize=0.001

# Put the in-map character/level select on the flat panel so the VR pointer works.
InGameMenuPanel=true

# Keep menu apparent size constant as resolution changes.
MenuScaleWithRes=true

# Aiming reticle shape: dot, cross, ring, ringdot or classic (GoldenEye's own
# crosshair: a ring with four spikes; drawn larger than the others).
VRReticleStyle=dot
# Aiming reticle colour: yellow, white, green, red or cyan.
VRReticleColor=white

# Force the menu panel opaque. Without this it goes see-through in a map.
ForceMenuOpaque=true

# Reticle horizontal correction. 0 = derive from the eye surface. Raise if it still looks tall.
VRReticleAspect=0

# Refresh the overlay capture every in-game frame. This also applies the menu
# alpha fix; turning it off can make menus look see-through/blurry.
AlwaysCaptureOverlay=false

# Console commands run once, ~1.5s after each map loads. Semicolon separated.
# These exist to hunt the in-game blur: the menu is sharp until the world
# loads and sharp again on the last frame before the game stops rendering,
# and Source's post-processing only runs while a 3D scene exists.
# Bisect by removing one at a time. Others worth trying:
#   mat_hdr_level 0          (disables HDR/bloom, changes lighting noticeably)
#   mat_bloomscale 0
#   mat_motion_blur_enabled 0
#   mat_filtertextures 1 ; mat_filterlightmaps 1
# If none of it helps, try $gesAA = 0 in Launch-GESVR.ps1 to rule out MSAA.
ExtraCvars=mat_software_aa_strength 0; mat_local_contrast_enable 0; mat_grain_scale_override 0

# Draw the 2D HUD in its own backbuffer pass rather than into the eye render
# targets, where it lands at the wrong size and in only one eye. Set false if
# the extra pass costs more than it is worth (the HUD then returns to the
# right eye, misplaced).
EyeHudPass=true

# Send the left eye's image to both eyes. No stereo depth, but a correct and
# sharp picture. Set false for true stereo once the right eye is fixed.
MonoEye=false

# Restore the old vertical crop convention (cropped the bottom where the eye
# needs the top, which pushed the whole view upward).
EyeCropLegacyV=true

# Diagnostic for the black right eye in stereo (MonoEye=false). Swaps which
# internal surface each eye captures into. If the black eye moves to the LEFT,
# the surface is at fault; if it stays on the right, the second capture is.
SwapEyeSurfaces=false

# Which texture feeds both eyes when MonoEye=true. 0 = left, 1 = right.
# 1 is a test: it shows the right texture alone, separating a bad texture
# from a bad two-texture submit. Set back to 0 for normal mono.
MonoEyeSource=0

# Render both eyes into ONE target, capturing each before the next pass
# overwrites it. Saves a colour and a depth buffer at no cost to resolution.
# Set false to go back to a separate target per eye.
SharedEyeTarget=false
